description: Local healthcare operations database covering billing, compliance, pharmacy, patient support, and medical dispatch domains.

patients.description: Master patient registry. One row per registered patient.

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format

blood_type.description: ABO blood group: A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-

insurance_provider.description: Name of the health insurance company

insurance_policy_number.description: Policy number issued by the insurer

patient_tier.description: Service tier: Standard | Premium | VIP. Affects SLA thresholds and compensation rules.

encounters.description: Clinical encounter records — each time a patient is seen by a physician. Links to billing claims.

department.description: Hospital department: Cardiology | Oncology | Orthopaedics | General Medicine | Emergency | Neurology | Dermatology | Gynaecology | Paediatrics | Radiology

primary_diagnosis_icd10.description: Primary diagnosis ICD-10-CM code (e.g. I10, J06.9, E11.9). This is the MAIN code used for billing.

secondary_diagnosis_icd10.description: Secondary/comorbidity ICD-10 code. May be NULL.

diagnosis_description.description: Plain-language description of the primary diagnosis

relationships.billing_claims: One encounter → many billing claims (via encounter_id)

billing_claims.description: Insurance billing claims submitted per encounter. Each claim has one CPT procedure code and links to an encounter with its ICD-10 diagnosis code.

procedure_description.description: Plain-language description of the billed procedure
procedure_description.example: Office visit, established patient, moderate complexity

claim_status.description: Current status: Pending | Approved | Rejected | UnderReview

rejection_reason.description: Free-text reason provided by the payer. NULL if not rejected.

has_coding_error.description: Boolean flag: 1 = coding error detected, 0 = clean. ~20% of claims have errors.

error_type.description: Type of coding error: CodeMismatch | MissingModifier | Unbundling | Upcoding. NULL if no error.

useful_aggregations: COUNT(*) WHERE claim_status = 'Rejected' — total rejected claims
SUM(claim_amount) WHERE claim_status = 'Pending' — pending revenue at risk
COUNT(*) WHERE has_coding_error = 1 — coding error volume
GROUP BY error_type — breakdown of error categories
GROUP BY payer_name, claim_status — rejection rate by payer

clinical_processes.description: Records of clinical procedures and administrative processes subject to compliance audit. Covers consent, documentation, protocol adherence.

process_type.description: Type of clinical process: Surgical Procedure | Patient Admission | Drug Administration | Blood Transfusion | ICU Transfer | Discharge Process | Radiology Order | Consent Procedure

patient_consent_obtained.description: Boolean: 1 = consent obtained, 0 = consent MISSING (JCI PFR.4 violation risk)

documentation_complete.description: Boolean: 1 = all documentation filed, 0 = documentation GAP (JCI COP.1 violation risk)

protocol_followed.description: Boolean: 1 = correct protocol followed, 0 = DEVIATION (SOP violation risk)

incident_reported.description: Boolean: 1 = incident report filed, 0 = not reported

audit_findings.description: Compliance audit results linked to clinical processes. Each finding represents a documented violation with severity and regulatory reference.

auditor_id.description: ID of the auditor who raised the finding

violation_type.description: Category of violation: DocumentationGap | ConsentMissing | ProtocolDeviation | ReportingFailure

severity.description: Violation severity: Critical | Major | Minor. Critical requires immediate action.

policy_reference.description: Specific section of the regulation, e.g. Section 4.12

finding_description.example: Consent form absent before blood transfusion procedure

resolved_at.description: Timestamp when resolved. NULL if still open.

useful_aggregations: GROUP BY regulation_body — breakdown by HIPAA vs JCI vs SOP
GROUP BY department JOIN clinical_processes — violations by department
COUNT(*) WHERE audit_date >= date('now', '-30 days') — recent violations

drugs.description: Master drug catalogue. One row per distinct drug product.

category.description: Therapeutic category: Antibiotic | Antidiabetic | Cardiovascular | Antihypertensive | Antiemetic | Gastrointestinal | Analgesic | Anticoagulant | Oncology | Corticosteroid | Respiratory | Vitamin

unit.description: Dispensing unit: tablets | vials | ml | mg | inhalers

relationships.drug_inventory: One drug → many inventory batches (via drug_id)

drug_inventory.description: Inventory batches for each drug. Multiple batches per drug with different expiry dates and stock levels. Use this table for expiry alerts and reorder triggers.

inventory_id.description: Unique inventory batch ID. Format: INV0000001

expiry_date.description: Expiry date. CRITICAL: compare to DATE('now') or julianday() for expiry alerts.

current_stock.description: Current quantity in stock (in dispensing units)

reorder_threshold.description: Stock level that triggers a reorder alert. Alert fires when current_stock < reorder_threshold.

max_stock_level.description: Maximum storage capacity for this item

average_daily_consumption.description: Average units consumed per day. Use for stockout estimation: current_stock / average_daily_consumption = days_until_stockout.

supplier_lead_time_days.description: Days from order to delivery by supplier

last_restocked.description: Date of most recent stock replenishment

useful_aggregations: WHERE julianday(expiry_date) - julianday('now') <= 60 — expiring within 60 days
WHERE current_stock < reorder_threshold               — below reorder threshold
ROUND(current_stock * unit_cost, 2) JOIN drugs        — stock value at risk

appointments.description: Scheduled and completed patient appointments. Used for SLA breach detection based on wait time vs category threshold.

appointment_category.description: Category defining SLA threshold: GP (30 min) | Specialist (45 min) | Emergency (15 min)

actual_start_datetime.description: Actual time the appointment started. Difference from scheduled = wait time.

wait_time_minutes.description: Pre-calculated wait time in minutes (actual_start - scheduled). Key field for SLA breach checks.

patient_complaints.description: Patient complaints about appointment wait times. Includes SLA breach assessment and compensation eligibility determination.

appointment_id.description: Foreign key to appointments (may be NULL)

complaint_text.example: Waited over an hour past scheduled time

sla_threshold_minutes.description: Applicable SLA threshold in minutes for the appointment category

sla_breached.description: Boolean: 1 = wait exceeded SLA threshold, 0 = within SLA

breach_severity.description: Severity of SLA breach: Critical (>2x threshold) | High | Medium | None

compensation_eligible.description: Boolean: 1 = patient qualifies for compensation under policy

compensation_type.description: Type of compensation: Voucher | Refund | Escalation | None

vehicles.description: Medical transport vehicle registry. Used for delivery assignment and availability checks.

vehicle_type.description: Vehicle type: Ambulance | Van | Motorcycle | Refrigerated

available.description: Boolean: 1 = vehicle available for assignment, 0 = deployed

base_location.description: Home base / depot location name in Delhi

routes.description: Predefined delivery routes between hospital locations in Delhi. traffic_factor multiplies base duration to get realistic ETA.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: Base estimated travel time in minutes (no traffic)

traffic_factor.description: Multiplier for peak-hour delays: 1.0 = no delay, 1.5 = 50% longer, 1.8 = severe congestion. Adjusted ETA = estimated_duration_minutes * traffic_factor.

delivery_records.description: Individual medical delivery records. Each record tracks a dispatch from origin to destination with SLA compliance data.

delivery_category.description: Priority category: Emergency (SLA 30 min) | Routine (SLA 120 min) | Refrigerated (SLA 60 min)

actual_delivery_datetime.description: Actual delivery completion time. NULL if not yet delivered.

sla_window_minutes.description: SLA time window in minutes: Emergency=30, Refrigerated=60, Routine=120

delivery_status.description: Current status: Scheduled | InTransit | Delivered | Delayed

sla_breached.description: Boolean: 1 = delivery exceeded SLA window, 0 = on time

delay_reason.description: Free-text reason for delay. NULL if on time.
delay_reason.example: Heavy traffic on NH-48 near Dhaula Kuan

useful_aggregations: COUNT(*) WHERE delivery_status = 'Delivered' AND sla_breached = 0 — on-time rate
estimated_duration_minutes * traffic_factor JOIN routes — adjusted ETA

join_patterns.billing_with_diagnosis: SELECT bc.*, e.primary_diagnosis_icd10, p.full_name FROM billing_claims bc JOIN encounters e ON bc.encounter_id = e.encounter_id JOIN patients p ON bc.patient_id = p.patient_id
join_patterns.compliance_with_department: SELECT af.*, cp.department, cp.process_type, cp.staff_name FROM audit_findings af JOIN clinical_processes cp ON af.process_id = cp.process_id
join_patterns.pharmacy_with_drug_details: SELECT di.*, d.drug_name, d.category, d.unit_cost, d.supplier FROM drug_inventory di JOIN drugs d ON di.drug_id = d.drug_id
join_patterns.complaints_with_patient_and_appt: SELECT pc.*, p.full_name, p.patient_tier, a.appointment_category, a.wait_time_minutes FROM patient_complaints pc JOIN patients p ON pc.patient_id = p.patient_id LEFT JOIN appointments a ON pc.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
join_patterns.delivery_with_route_and_vehicle: SELECT dr.*, r.origin, r.destination, r.distance_km, r.traffic_factor, ROUND(r.estimated_duration_minutes * r.traffic_factor) AS adjusted_eta, v.vehicle_type, v.registration FROM delivery_records dr JOIN routes r ON dr.route_id = r.route_id JOIN vehicles v ON dr.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id

query_rules: ALWAYS use SELECT only. Never INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DROP.
ALWAYS use parameterised placeholders (?) for any user-supplied values.
For expiry date comparisons use: julianday(expiry_date) - julianday('now')
For date range queries use: DATE('now', '-N days') or DATE('now', '+N days')
Default LIMIT is 50 rows. Use aggregate queries (COUNT, SUM, AVG) for summary questions.
For adjusted ETA always multiply: estimated_duration_minutes * traffic_factor
For days until stockout calculate: ROUND(current_stock / average_daily_consumption)
Boolean columns (has_coding_error, sla_breached, available, etc.) store 1 for TRUE and 0 for FALSE
